simulation.note: Pass 1 draws fresh crypto.randomBytes seeds per configuration, so npm run simulate with no saved seeds runs a new experiment with different numbers. Each row of outputs/simulation-results.json stores the seed pair it was produced with: Step 16 (inside npm test) and npm run replay re-execute the committed experiment from those seeds and require every derived quantity to reproduce, writing nothing, and npm run regen regenerates the file with src/simulate.ts from the same saved seeds so that npm run diff-simulation can compare it with the committed file field by field. The file carries no generatedAt and no executionTimeMs, so a regeneration on the machine that produced it is byte-identical; on another machine one p-value can differ in its last digit, which the field comparison tolerates.
